title: JEE Mains — Physics Mock Test (Mechanics)
description: Full chapter mock test on Mechanics for JEE Mains preparation. Covers kinematics, Newton's laws, work-energy theorem.
subject: physics
instructions: Each wrong answer carries -1 mark (negative marking).

questions.question: A particle moves in a straight line with uniform acceleration. If it covers distances s₁ and s₂ in the first and second seconds respectively, the acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Using s = ut + ½at², the difference in distances in consecutive seconds equals the acceleration.
questions.hint: Use the equation for distance in nth second.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with velocity 20 m/s. The maximum height reached is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Using v² = u² - 2gh, at max height v=0: h = u²/2g = 400/20 = 20 m.

questions.question: Two forces of 3 N and 4 N act at right angles to each other. The resultant force is:
questions.hint: Use Pythagoras theorem for perpendicular vectors.

questions.question: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with velocity 3 m/s. A force of 4 N acts on it for 2 seconds. The final velocity is:
questions.hint: Find acceleration first, then use v = u + at.

questions.question: The work done by a force of 10 N in displacing a body by 5 m at 60° to the force is:
A body of mass 5 kg is raised to a height of 10 m. Its potential energy is (g = 10 m/s²):
The coefficient of friction between two surfaces is 0.4. The normal force is 50 N. The frictional force is:
A projectile is fired at 45° to the horizontal. The ratio of horizontal range to maximum height is:
questions.explanation: R = u²sin2θ/g, H = u²sin²θ/2g. At θ=45°: R/H = 4.
questions.hint: Use projectile motion formulas for R and H.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body is increased by 44%. Its momentum increases by:
questions.explanation: KE = p²/2m. If KE increases by 44%, p increases by √1.44 - 1 = 1.2 - 1 = 20%.

questions.question: A body is in equilibrium under three concurrent forces. Which condition must be satisfied?

options.text: The forces must be equal in magnitude
The vector sum of all forces must be zero
The forces must act in the same direction
The forces must be perpendicular to each other

questions.explanation: For equilibrium, the net force (vector sum) must be zero: ΣF = 0.
